angle: Buyer-side and event records: NHTSA Part 573 recall reports (found by web search, then the NHTSA recall flat-file index FLAT_RCL_POST_2010 filtered to 2021-2026 trailer/chassis/light-tower/generator vehicle recalls and trailer-component equipment recalls), military/federal contract award notices (Army, USMC, Navy, DLA), trade-show exhibitor records (MATS 2026 spotlight, Equine Affaire Ohio, Quarter Horse Congress, Farm Progress, NFMS, World of Concrete, boat shows, HDAW), rental-fleet and oilfield case studies. Each manufacturer resolved to plant(s) through its own website or trade press, quotes checked with fetch_page.py --check.
searches_until_dry: Web-search discovery went dry: the last 2 discovery searches (22-23) produced no new manufacturer, and exhibitor-list and case-study angles were dry after 1-2 tries each. The NHTSA recall index did not go dry; it listed about 60 more trailer filers than could be resolved within budget. So overall the list is not at a dry point.

notes.method: The NHTSA flat file is the index of Part 573 recall filings. Using it in bulk goes beyond 'found by web search'; this is disclosed here and in each found_via. The flat file lacks some 2026 campaigns (26V542 and 26V291 were missing), so those came from PDFs found by web search. Part 573 addresses are filer addresses. They count as plant evidence only where the Component Manufacturer block shows the same company and address for a welded frame part. Elsewhere they are marked company-level only.
notes.plant_confirmed_rule: True only when the quoted page ties in-definition production or welding to the city. Records resting only on an address line, a corporate HQ, or a contract-award contractor city are kept with plant_confirmed=false.
notes.job_postings: Stoughton's careers page was used only to confirm welding at sites already found via the recall index. It was not a discovery method.

blind_spots: Recall records only show makers that filed a recall and certify complete trailers. Component plants (suspensions, axles, hitches, landing gear) mostly file equipment recalls only for consumer parts, so heavy-truck component plants are under-sampled.
Makers with no recall in 2021-2026 are invisible to this method. That includes many small regional livestock, flatbed and oilfield trailer shops and most mobile-power makers, which seldom file.
Military awards cover only a handful of defense trailer and generator primes.
Show exhibitor pages were mostly partial spotlights or dealer-heavy (Equine Affaire listed dealers), so they added almost nothing.
Multi-plant parents are resolved only where the company's own page lists its plants. Several big van and reefer makers (Utility, Great Dane, Wabash, Hyundai Translead) are left at company level.
Many trailer-maker sites are JavaScript-only or reset connections, which blocked plant confirmation (Trailstar, Trails West, Reitnouer, Virnig, PJ, Big Tex contact pages).
